lines.speaker: Nireus
lines.text: Look, here's Menippus—he can judge which of us is better-looking. Tell him, Menippus. Aren't I the handsome one?

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Who are you two? I should probably know that first.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Right. And which one is Nireus, and which one is Thersites? [pause] Because it's still not obvious.

lines.speaker: Thersites
lines.text: [laughs] Well, that's one point for me already! We look exactly the same. It turns out you aren't vastly superior just because that blind guy Homer praised you and called you the most beautiful man in the world. I've got a pointy skull, I'm entirely bald, and the judge thinks we're twins. But go on, Menippus, take a good look and tell us who's prettier.

lines.speaker: Nireus
lines.text: Me! The son of Aglaia and Charopus! The most beautiful man who ever went to Troy!

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Yes, well, you didn't come under the earth as the most beautiful man, as far as I can tell. The bones are identical. Honestly, the only way I could tell your skull apart from Thersites' is that yours looks incredibly brittle. It's very delicate. Not very manly.

lines.speaker: Nireus
lines.text: Just ask Homer what I looked like when I sailed with the Achaeans!

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: You're talking about dreams. I am looking at what you have right now. What you had then is strictly the business of the people back then.

lines.speaker: Nireus
lines.text: [pause] So I am not the better-looking one down here, Menippus?

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Neither of you is good-looking. Nobody is. It is absolute equality in Hades. We all look exactly the same.

lines.speaker: Thersites
lines.text: [chuckles] That is entirely good enough for me.
